requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify borrower citizenship eligibility and the program’s first-time-homebuyer and guarantor requirements. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the borrower meets the stated citizenship and homeownership eligibility requirements.

## Step
Check whether the borrower is a US Citizen or Permanent Resident.

## Step
If the borrower is a Permanent Resident, verify an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89.

## Step
Check whether the application is for a First Time Homebuyer. Acra defines a First Time Home Buyer as “an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property)”.

## Step
Verify that at least one guarantor has prior homeownership experience and that at least one borrower / guarantor attests on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer. Applicability of the guarantor requirements to individual borrowers as well as entities is part of Q-13.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The borrower’s citizenship type is US Citizen or Permanent Resident.
- If the borrower is a Permanent Resident, the borrower has an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89.
- The application is not a First Time Homebuyer application.
- At least one guarantor has prior homeownership experience.
- At least one borrower / guarantor attests on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable step is met and every check holds.
- **Conditional**: Eligibility requirements are otherwise met, subject to obtaining required documentation, attestation, or Acra confirmation that must be cleared.
- **Fail**: The borrower is not a US Citizen or Permanent Resident, the application is for a First Time Homebuyer, or an applicable requirement is not met.
- **Not Applicable**: This job does not apply to the case.

values.skill: Apply the stated decisioning-score selection and minimum-score rules, then verify the applicable tradeline requirement.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Apply the stated decisioning-score selection and minimum-score rules, then verify the applicable tradeline requirement. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the applicant’s decisioning score and tradelines meet the Platinum Summary requirements.

## Step
For a loan that does not close in the name of an entity, identify the Primary Wage Earner middle score as the decisioning credit score.

## Step
For a loan that closes in the name of an entity, use the highest middle score of the personal guarantors, presuming equal percentages of ownership. If ownership percentages differ, use the individual with the highest concentration of ownership.

## Step
Check that the decisioning credit score is at least 700.

## Step
Apply the tradeline rule: applicants with scores from 3 repositories are acceptable with no tradeline overlay; applicants with 2 or fewer scores require 2 tradelines & 24 month history or 3 tradelines & 12 month history.

## Step
If the case has one score, treat it as within “2 or fewer scores” for the tradeline requirement. Do not infer a decisioning-score rule for one or two scores, a no-score pathway, how to identify the Primary Wage Earner without income documentation, or which score to use when two or more guarantors hold an equal largest ownership interest and ownership is not equal across all guarantors; those matters require Acra confirmation (Q-05).

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The decisioning credit score is the Primary Wage Earner middle score, or, for an entity loan, the score selected using the stated personal-guarantor and ownership rule.
- The decisioning credit score is at least 700.
- Applicants with scores from 3 repositories are treated as acceptable with no tradeline overlay, and applicants with 2 or fewer scores meet 2 tradelines & 24 month history or 3 tradelines & 12 month history.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable step is met and every check holds.
- **Conditional**: The requirements are otherwise met, subject to obtaining missing score, ownership, income, or tradeline information, or Acra confirmation that must be cleared.
- **Fail**: The decisioning score is below 700 or an applicable tradeline requirement is not met.
- **Not Applicable**: This job does not apply to the case.

# Apply the stated escrow-waiver requirements only when an escrow waiver is requested. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether a requested escrow waiver meets the printed loan-amount, mortgage-history, and Section 35 requirements.

## Step
If no escrow waiver is requested, stop; this job does not apply.

## Step
For a requested waiver, verify that the loan amount does not exceed $1.5M.

## Step
Verify “0x30x24 Mortgage History required”.

## Step
Verify that the loan is not a Section 35 loan. “Section 35” is not defined in the sources; Acra confirmation is requested (Q-14). Do not apply a CLTV or FICO limit, as none is printed for the Platinum waiver.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- If an escrow waiver is requested, the loan amount is no more than $1.5M.
- If an escrow waiver is requested, the required “0x30x24 Mortgage History” is met.
- If an escrow waiver is requested, the loan is not a Section 35 loan.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: An escrow waiver is requested and every applicable step is met and every check holds.
- **Conditional**: An escrow waiver is requested and the requirements are otherwise met, subject to obtaining required mortgage-history information or Acra clarification that must be cleared.
- **Fail**: An escrow waiver is requested and the loan amount exceeds $1.5M, the required mortgage history is not met, or the loan is a Section 35 loan.
- **Not Applicable**: No escrow waiver is requested.

values.skill: Review the required mortgage or rental history scope and apply the stated rules for matured loans.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Review the required mortgage or rental history scope and apply the stated rules for matured loans. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the mortgage / rental rating review uses the required properties and history period, including the DSCR documentation scope.

## Step
For determining mortgage pricing, evaluate ratings for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months.

## Step
Consider all reported mortgages on credit. Where the applicant has mortgages that are not reported, review documentation for the applicant’s primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property.

## Step
For DSCR loans, require documentation on the subject property, principal residence, and second home (if any) of the borrower and / or guarantor(s). Require payment history for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable. Additional properties do not require housing history to be documented unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred, for example a foreclosure listing the borrower (individually or as guarantor) on the credit report.

## Step
For a loan that has matured, rate it based on the maturity date of the loan; any extensions of the maturity date must be in writing.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- Mortgage / rental ratings for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months have been evaluated.
- All reported mortgages on credit have been considered, and documentation is present to evaluate history on primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property where the applicant has mortgages that are not reported.
- For a DSCR loan, documentation and payment history cover the subject property, primary residence, and second home (if any) of the borrower and / or guarantor(s), with additional-property housing history documented when file documents suggest a major credit event has occurred.
- A matured loan is rated based on its maturity date, and any extension of the maturity date is in writing.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable step is met and every check holds.
- **Conditional**: The requirements are otherwise met, subject to obtaining required payment-history, mortgage, maturity-date, or written-extension documentation that must be cleared.
- **Fail**: An applicable history-scope or matured-loan requirement is not met.
- **Not Applicable**: This job does not apply to the case.

values.skill: Apply the stated rent numerator, PITIA denominator, and channel minimum without resolving open policy questions.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Apply the stated rent numerator, PITIA denominator, and channel minimum without resolving open policy questions. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine the qualifying DSCR and whether it meets the minimum for the loan channel.

## Step
Confirm the transaction is a DSCR transaction and identify whether the rental income is long-term or short-term.

## Step
Use the greater of market rent as established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent, as the qualifying rent.

## Step
If actual rent is used, verify evidence of 2 months’ proof of receipts and that the lease is in place for at least 3 months after loan closing.

## Step
Calculate the denominator using annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (collectively, ‘PITIA’); include subordinate financing, if applicable.

## Step
Use the first payment due under the terms of the Note when calculating the DSCR. If the loan is interest-only, do not decide which payment enters the denominator; that question is identified as Q-21.

## Step
Compare the resulting DSCR with the applicable channel minimum: Correspondent ≥ 1.2; Wholesale ≥ 1.0.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The rental income used to qualify is long-term, not short-term.
- The qualifying rent is the greater of market rent established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent.
- If actual rent is used, evidence documents 2 months’ proof of receipts.
- If actual rent is used, the lease is in place for at least 3 months after loan closing.
- The denominator includes annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees, and includes subordinate financing if applicable.
- The DSCR calculation uses the first payment due under the terms of the Note.
- The DSCR is at least the applicable channel minimum: Correspondent ≥ 1.2; Wholesale ≥ 1.0.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable step is met and every check holds.
- **Conditional**: The applicable requirements are met subject to conditions that must be cleared.
- **Fail**: A required step is not met or a check does not hold.
- **Not Applicable**: The case is not a DSCR transaction.

values.skill: Check required rent schedules and, when lease rent is excessive, supporting evidence that the rent is typical for the area.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Check required rent schedules and, when lease rent is excessive, supporting evidence that the rent is typical for the area. - Base Version

## Purpose

Confirm the required 1007 and any applicable documentation supporting lease rent.

## Step
For a DSCR qualifying file, verify that a Single-Family Comparable Rent Schedule (FNMA Form 1007) is provided.

## Step
Verify that the 1007 is from the original appraiser or a state licensed appraiser.

## Step
For a lease-option purchase where the down payment required in §3.45 is generated from excess monthly rent contributions, verify that a 1007 is provided.

## Step
When proposed rental income is being used to qualify, verify that a 1007 is provided.

## Step
For a single family investment property with excessive monthly rent payments reflected on the lease, review documentation supporting that the monthly rent is typical for the area. Acceptable documentation may include classified ads from local newspapers, a 1007 completed by the appraiser, or a market rent survey completed by a local real estate company or rental management company familiar with market rents in the area.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- A Single-Family Comparable Rent Schedule (FNMA Form 1007) is provided for the DSCR qualifying file.
- The 1007 is from the original appraiser or a state licensed appraiser.
- If the transaction is a lease-option purchase and the down payment required in §3.45 is generated from excess monthly rent contributions, a 1007 is provided.
- If proposed rental income is being used to qualify, a 1007 is provided.
- If a single family investment property's lease reflects excessive monthly rent payments, documentation supports that the monthly rent is typical for the area.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable step is met and every check holds.
- **Conditional**: The applicable requirements are met subject to conditions that must be cleared.
- **Fail**: A required step is not met or a check does not hold.
- **Not Applicable**: The case is not a DSCR qualifying file and none of the other stated 1007 triggers applies.

values.skill: Verify the currency and scope of the required borrower and guarantor due diligence and background review.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify the currency and scope of the required borrower and guarantor due diligence and background review. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether due diligence meets PLAT-5.11 and whether the required parties are included in the background review described in PLAT-5.12.

## Step
Determine the date of loan approval or draw and verify that Borrower / Guarantor Due Diligence is current as of that date.

## Step
For an entity borrower, identify the entity, recourse guarantor(s), every party (individual or entity) owning 20% or more of the entity directly or indirectly, and every party with managing control.

## Step
For individual borrowers, identify all such individuals.

## Step
Verify that the background review covers the applicable Key Principals and Entities. The review may be ordered from Checkpoint, LexisNexis or another comparable provider and may include criminal history, OFAC searches, litigation, judgment, and lien searches.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- Borrower / Guarantor Due Diligence is current as of the date of any loan approval or draw.
- For an entity borrower, the background-review scope includes the entity, recourse guarantor(s), all direct or indirect owners of 20% or more, and parties with managing control.
- For individual borrowers, the background-review scope includes all such individuals.
- The background review is of the Key Principals and Entities described in PLAT-5.12.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Due diligence is current as of the applicable approval or draw date and the background-review scope includes the applicable Key Principals and Entities.
- **Conditional**: A due-diligence or background-review requirement remains subject to a condition that must be cleared.
- **Fail**: Due diligence is not current as of the applicable date or the required parties are not included in the review scope.
- **Not Applicable**: The case has no borrower or guarantor due-diligence review to perform.

values.skill: Compare the borrower’s stated citizenship and first-time homebuyer status with the stated eligibility requirements.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Compare the borrower’s stated citizenship and first-time homebuyer status with the stated eligibility requirements. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the borrower meets the citizenship and first-time homebuyer requirements stated in PLAT-4.1 through PLAT-4.4.

## Step
Check whether the borrower is a US Citizen or Permanent Resident.

## Step
If the borrower is a Permanent Resident, verify an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89.

## Step
Determine whether the application meets Acra’s definition of a First Time Home Buyer: all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property).

## Step
Apply the stated ineligibility of First Time Homebuyers for this program.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The borrower’s citizenship type is US Citizen or Permanent Resident.
- For a Permanent Resident, the PRA ID is unexpired and an SSA card / SSA-89 is provided.
- The borrower is not a First Time Homebuyer under Acra’s stated definition.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The borrower has an eligible citizenship type, satisfies the Permanent Resident document requirement if applicable, and is not a First Time Homebuyer.
- **Conditional**: An applicable requirement remains subject to a condition that must be cleared.
- **Fail**: The borrower has a citizenship type not listed as eligible, fails an applicable Permanent Resident document requirement, or is a First Time Homebuyer.
- **Not Applicable**: This borrower eligibility review does not apply to the case.

values.skill: Review the required entity documents and verify that each specified document and content requirement is satisfied.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Review the required entity documents and verify that each specified document and content requirement is satisfied. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the entity documentation required by PLAT-5.10 is complete and acceptable for review under the stated requirements.

## Step
Obtain a complete, legible Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments.

## Step
For LLCs and Partnerships, obtain a complete, legible Operating Agreement with all referenced exhibits and all amendments; for corporations, obtain the Bylaws with all referenced exhibits and all amendments. Verify that the document states whether the entity is member or manager managed, authorizes borrowing money and entering into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Determine whether additional information is required if formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

## Step
Obtain documentation evidencing all ownership interests. For LLCs and Partnerships, verify that the Operating Agreement identifies by name all persons and their ownership interest or attaches that information as an exhibit, or that membership interest certificates / units are provided in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

## Step
For S or C Corporations, obtain shareholder / stockholder certificates complying with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation’s stock ledger. Verify that the certificate or ledger accounts for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, obtain an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate.

## Step
For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, obtain the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest and a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest; if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed, verify that the letter includes a statement to that effect.

## Step
Verify that names on entity documents match the identification; if they do not match exactly, obtain a letter of explanation addressing the discrepancy.

## Step
Obtain a Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

## Step
If the entity is formed in a state other than where business is conducted or the property is located, obtain a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted.

## Step
Obtain the entity’s IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter. If an EIN exception is requested, verify that it is submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

## Step
Obtain a Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. Check whether the Operating Agreement or Bylaws require it even where ownership is held by one individual. Do not accept it to designate a signor on a personal guarantee.

## Step
If an attorney in fact is designated to execute a personal guarantee, verify that the principal utilizes a Power of Attorney for that designation.

## Step
Record any additional supporting documentation Legal conditions for in its sole discretion.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- A complete, legible Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments are provided.
- The applicable Operating Agreement or Bylaws and all referenced exhibits and amendments are provided and contain the required management, borrowing, contracting, and signer provisions.
- Documentation evidences all ownership interests in the manner required for the entity type.
- The applicable corporate share evidence accounts for all outstanding shares, and an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is provided when required.
- When both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable for an S-corporation or Partnership, the required K-1 statements and CPA or Tax Preparer letter are provided, including the required statement if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.
- Names on entity documents match identification, or a letter of explanation addresses any exact-name discrepancy.
- A Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent is valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.
- Where applicable, qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted is documented.
- The entity’s IRS Form SS4 or TIN or EIN issuance letter is provided, or an EIN exception request with the required grounds letter is submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department.
- The required Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution is signed by all members, authorizes the transaction, and identifies the authorized loan-document signatory; it is not used to designate a personal-guarantee signor.
- A Power of Attorney is utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee, where applicable.
- Any additional supporting documentation required by Legal in its sole discretion is provided.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable required document and content requirement is satisfied, and any additional documentation required by Legal is provided.
- **Conditional**: Documentation is subject to a condition, including an EIN exception request or additional supporting documentation required by Legal, that must be cleared.
- **Fail**: A required document or content requirement is not satisfied, or a borrower letter is offered in place of a required document.
- **Not Applicable**: The case has no entity documentation requirement under this job.

values.skill: Verify the entity, ownership structure, required guarantors, and related eligibility conditions against the stated requirements.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify the entity, ownership structure, required guarantors, and related eligibility conditions against the stated requirements. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether an entity borrower and its ownership and guarantee arrangements meet PLAT-5.1 through PLAT-5.9.

## Step
Determine whether the transaction is business purpose and concerns an investment property exclusively.

## Step
Confirm that collateral title will be held directly by individual person(s) or by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion.

## Step
For an entity borrower, identify every direct and indirect owner, each ownership percentage, and any party with managing control; determine which individuals have direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20%.

## Step
Verify that every individual with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% provides an Acra-approved recourse guarantee or Exhibit 7. If there are multiple guarantors, verify that recourse is joint and several.

## Step
Verify that the entity borrower is a single purpose entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties and is engaged in owning and operating residential investment or rental properties; verify that it is not a series limited liability company.

## Step
Identify every entity that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and be on title as a direct owner; verify that each is a borrowing entity.

## Step
Review operating-agreement or bylaw changes affecting ownership percentages and their timing in relation to the Application Date and application process; do not recognize changes made with intent to circumvent required personal guarantors or changes within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process.

## Step
Verify that the entity is a US formed and based Entity and is not a foreign owned entity; verify that its type is one of the allowed types and is not a prohibited type.

## Step
Check that the structure does not involve a prohibited business entity arrangement: nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary owned by individual(s), and multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.

## Step
Verify that at least one guarantor has prior homeownership experience and that at least one borrower / guarantor attests on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The transaction is a business purpose transaction involving an investment property exclusively.
- Collateral title is held directly by individual person(s) or by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion.
- Every individual with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% provides an Acra-approved recourse guarantee or Exhibit 7.
- Where there are multiple guarantors, all recourse is joint and several.
- The entity borrower is a single purpose entity as defined in PLAT-5.4 and is not a series limited liability company.
- Every entity that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and be on title as a direct owner is a borrowing entity.
- No ownership-percentage change with intent to circumvent required personal guarantors is recognized, and no such change is made within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process.
- The entity is US formed and based, is not foreign owned, and is of an allowed type rather than a prohibited type.
- The entity ownership structure complies with the stated one-subsidiary limit and does not involve multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera.
- At least one guarantor has prior homeownership experience.
- At least one borrower / guarantor attests on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable step is met and every check holds.
- **Conditional**: The applicable requirements are met subject to conditions that must be cleared.
- **Fail**: An applicable step is not met or a check does not hold.
- **Not Applicable**: There is no entity borrower or other entity arrangement to which this job applies.

values.skill: Review trust documents and terms against each stated requirement for permitted title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Review trust documents and terms against each stated requirement for permitted title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust meets PLAT-5.13.

## Step
Determine whether title is to be vested in an inter vivos revocable trust; if so, obtain a complete, legible copy of the Trust or a Certification of Trust containing every item specified in PLAT-5.13.

## Step
Verify that the Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established and is revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime.

## Step
Verify that the Trust is established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly, and becomes effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

## Step
Verify that the primary beneficiary is the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

## Step
If the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same, obtain written exception by Acra Senior Management.

## Step
Verify that the Trust specifies the Trustee’s power to hold title and mortgage the property; the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money or that consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

## Step
Record any additional supporting documentation Legal conditions for in its sole discretion.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust or a Certification of Trust states the existence and date of the Trust; Trustor(s) and current Trustee(s); Trustee powers; whether the Trust is revocable and, if so, who holds the right to revoke; required Trustee signers; Trust identification number; how title to Trust assets should be taken; and that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.
- The Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established and is revocable as specified.
- The Trust is established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly, and becomes effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.
- The primary beneficiary of the Trust is the individual(s) establishing the Trust.
- If the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same, written exception by Acra Senior Management is obtained.
- The Trust contains all required provisions concerning the Trustee’s powers, beneficiary consent to borrowing, unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights, and the lender's rights as a creditor.
- Any additional supporting documentation required by Legal in its sole discretion is provided.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Title is vested in an inter vivos revocable trust and every applicable requirement is met, including any additional documentation required by Legal.
- **Conditional**: A required written exception or other applicable condition remains to be obtained or cleared.
- **Fail**: An applicable trust requirement is not met, including where the trust is irrevocable.
- **Not Applicable**: Title is not vested in an inter vivos revocable trust.

values.skill: Apply the printed escrow-waiver limits and separately check the stated impound requirement for a property listed for sale.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Apply the printed escrow-waiver limits and separately check the stated impound requirement for a property listed for sale. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether a requested escrow waiver meets the stated loan amount and mortgage-history requirements, account for the undefined Section 35 exclusion, and address the separate impound requirement for a property listed for sale.

## Step
If an escrow waiver is requested, check that the loan amount does not exceed $1.5M.

## Step
If an escrow waiver is requested, check for 0x30x24 Mortgage History.

## Step
If an escrow waiver is requested, determine whether the loan is a Section 35 loan; Section 35 loans are ineligible, but Section 35 is not defined in the source, so obtain Acra confirmation as needed.

## Step
Separately, if the property is listed for sale, require impounds.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- If escrow_waiver_requested is true, loan_amount <= $1,500,000.
- If escrow_waiver_requested is true, mortgage_history_0x30x24 is true.

# Identify each stated reserve trigger and verify the corresponding reserve amount without assuming unstated rules. - Base Version

## Purpose

Assess the reserve requirements stated for CLTV, property listed for sale, recent forbearance or mortgage lates with tenant occupancy, and unavailable rent loss insurance.

## Step
If CLTV is greater than 75.00%, check for 6-months Reserves required for CLTV > 75.00%.

## Step
If the property was listed for sale within six months, check for twenty-four (24) months of reserves. Cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide.

## Step
Determine whether the property is tenant-occupied and whether there was forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months without timely receipt of the prior two months' rent. If so, check for 12 months of the subject's payment in reserve; this may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand. The relationship to 0x30x12 is unresolved in the source.

## Step
If rent loss insurance is required but cannot be obtained, check for two (2) months reserves for every one (1) month of coverage not provided.

## Step
Do not assume a base reserve requirement at CLTV of 75.00% or below, a payment basis, permitted sources, whether overlapping triggers are cumulative, or whether reserves substituted for rent loss insurance are additional; obtain Acra confirmation.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- If cltv_pct > 75.00%, reserves_months >= 6.
- If listed_for_sale_last_6_months is true, reserves_months >= 24.
- If there was forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, the subject is tenant-occupied, and the prior two months' rent was not received timely, 12 months of the subject's payment are held in reserve.
- If rent loss insurance is required but cannot be obtained, reserves equal two (2) months for every one (1) month of coverage not provided.
- The base reserve requirement at CLTV of 75.00% or below, payment basis, permitted sources, cumulative treatment of overlapping triggers, and treatment of reserves substituted for rent loss insurance as additional reserves have been confirmed by Acra where applicable.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable reserve trigger is identified, each corresponding reserve check holds, and all applicable unresolved reserve terms have been confirmed by Acra.
- **Conditional**: No applicable reserve check is known to fail, but trigger facts, reserve amounts, or applicable Acra confirmations remain outstanding.
- **Fail**: Any applicable reserve check does not hold.
- **Not Applicable**: No stated reserve trigger applies and no unresolved base reserve requirement applies to the case.

# Identify each applicable published CLTV cap and check the case CLTV against it. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether CLTV meets the matrix and the additional stated limits and adjustments.

## Step
Apply the matrix row for the decisioning score and loan purpose: 730 and above, 80% for Purchase, 80% for Rate & Term, and 75% for Cash-Out; 721 through 729, 80%, 80%, and 65%, respectively; 700 through 720 on a literal reading of the printed thresholds, 80%, 80%, and 55%, respectively.

## Step
Apply the 75.00% maximum CLTV when the loan amount is less than $350,000 or greater than $1,500,000.

## Step
Apply the 75.00% maximum CLTV for a Warrantable Condo or Two-Units property.

## Step
Apply the 75.00% maximum CLTV for Interest-Only (5 Yr Term).

## Step
Apply the 65% LTV / CLTV maximum when the property was listed for sale within six months.

## Step
For Correspondent loans with a score of 700-719, apply the stated 60% CLTV restriction; for a cash-out loan in that score range, do not use that restriction to raise the matrix’s 55% limit.

## Step
For a declining-market property, account for the stated -5% CLTV adjustment and obtain confirmation of how it combines with other caps.

## Step
Where the score is 720, or the Correspondent 700-719 restriction interacts with the matrix by purpose, obtain the requested Acra confirmation on treatment of the printed 721 threshold and the limits.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- cltv_pct does not exceed the matrix maximum for the decisioning score and loan_purpose, using the printed thresholds literally.
- If loan_amount is less than $350,000 or greater than $1,500,000, cltv_pct does not exceed 75.00%.
- If property_type is Warrantable Condo or Two-Units, cltv_pct does not exceed 75.00%.
- If product_is_interest_only is true, cltv_pct does not exceed 75.00%.
- If listed_for_sale_last_6_months is true, cltv_pct does not exceed 65%.
- If channel is Correspondent and the decisioning score is from 700 through 719, cltv_pct does not exceed 60%; a cash-out case in this range must also meet the matrix maximum.
- If the property is in a declining market, the -5% CLTV adjustment is applied using the combination with other caps confirmed by Acra.
- If the case has a score of 720, or is a Correspondent case with a score of 700-719, the applicable Q-01 treatment has been confirmed by Acra.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable CLTV check holds, and any applicable Q-01 or Q-08 treatment has been confirmed and applied.
- **Conditional**: A Q-01 or Q-08 confirmation or declining-market profile needed to determine the applicable CLTV limit is pending.
- **Fail**: Any applicable CLTV check does not hold.
- **Not Applicable**: The case has no CLTV limit to assess.

Do not infer that a state not listed, or a case that does not match a listed condition, has no other prepayment restriction.

- The property state is AK and the property is Residential 1-4.
- The property state is IL and the loan is to an ENTITY OR INDIVIDUAL, is Residential 1-4, and the loan amount is ≤$250,000.
- The property state is IL and the loan is to an INDIVIDUAL, is Residential 1-4, the loan amount is >$250,000, and the interest rate is >8%.
- The property state is KS and the property is Residential 1-4.
- The property state is MD.
- The property state is MI and the property is Residential 1-4.
- The property state is MN and the property is Residential 1-4.
- The property state is MS and the property is Residential 1 unit.
- The property state is NJ and the loan is closing in the name of an INDIVIDUAL.

- The property state is VT and the loan amount is <$1 Million.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: No printed state restriction condition matches the case. This does not establish that no other restriction applies.
- **Conditional**: A printed state restriction condition matches the case, but what “BUY-OUT” requires or whether the actual prepayment arrangement meets the restriction remains unresolved.

## Purpose

Determine whether applicable one- to four-unit non-owner occupied income-property requirements are met.

For a borrower purchasing or refinancing a one- to four-family investment property, verify execution of the One- to Four-Family Rider with the loan documents.

Apply the stated exemption for loans with ≤ 70% CLTV and leave the LTV-at-or-below-70% / CLTV-above-70% case unresolved pending Acra confirmation.

If rent loss insurance is required but cannot be obtained, verify the permitted reserve substitution for each month of coverage not provided.

- A borrower purchasing or refinancing a one- to four-family investment property executes a One- to Four-Family Rider with the loan documents.

- A loan with ≤ 70% CLTV is not required to carry rent loss insurance.
- The LTV-at-or-below-70% and CLTV-above-70% case is resolved by Acra confirmation.
- When required rent loss insurance cannot be obtained, the borrower provides two (2) months reserves for every one (1) month of rent loss coverage not provided.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable Rider and rent loss insurance requirement is met, including any permitted reserve substitution.
- **Conditional**: A required Rider, insurance coverage, reserve substitution, or Acra confirmation is pending.

- citizenship_type is one of: US Citizen, Permanent Resident, Non-Permanent Resident, Foreign National, ITIN.

## Step
Check that the borrower is not Foreign National.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- If an escrow waiver is requested, loan amount is no greater than $1.5M.
- If an escrow waiver is requested, CLTV is no greater than 80%.
- If an escrow waiver is requested, FICO is at least 700.
- If an escrow waiver is requested, mortgage history is no worse than 0x30x24.
- If an escrow waiver is requested, the borrower is not Foreign National.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: An escrow waiver is not requested, or every stated escrow waiver requirement holds.
- **Conditional**: met, subject to conditions that must be cleared
- **Fail**: An escrow waiver is requested and any stated escrow waiver requirement does not hold.
- **Not Applicable**: An escrow waiver is not requested.

values.skill: Check the mortgage and rental history documentation against the stated property scope and review period.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Check the mortgage and rental history documentation against the stated property scope and review period. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the history needed to evaluate mortgage pricing and DSCR payment history has been documented for the properties specified by the guidelines.

## Step
Evaluate the ratings for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months.

## Step
Consider all reported mortgages on credit.

## Step
Where the applicant has mortgages that are not reported, check that the file contains documentation to evaluate history on the applicant's primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property.

## Step
For DSCR loans, check documentation on the subject property, principal residence, and second home (if any) of the borrower and / or guarantor(s).

## Step
For DSCR loans, do not require housing history documentation for additional properties unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred.

## Step
For DSCR loans, check payment history for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable.

## Step
For loans that have matured, rate the loan based on the maturity date; check that any extensions of the maturity date are in writing.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- Ratings for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months are evaluated.
- All reported mortgages on credit are considered.
- Where mortgages are not reported, the file contains documentation to evaluate history on the applicant's primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property.
- For a DSCR loan, documentation covers the subject property, principal residence, and second home (if any) of the borrower and / or guarantor(s).
- For a DSCR loan, additional properties are not required to have housing history documented unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred.
- For a DSCR loan, payment history is available for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable.
- For a loan that has matured, the rating is based on the maturity date and any extension of the maturity date is in writing.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable documentation and rating check holds.
- **Conditional**: Required history, payment-history, maturity, or extension information is not available for review.
- **Fail**: An applicable documentation or rating requirement is not met.
- **Not Applicable**: the job does not apply to this case

values.skill: Compare reported score and tradeline information with the applicable credit requirements.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Compare reported score and tradeline information with the applicable credit requirements. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the score and tradeline requirements are met, apply the stated overlays when applicable, and verify the reserve requirement for FICO below 620.

## Step
Review the number of repositories reporting scores and the tradeline information.

## Step
If there are scores from 3 repositories, apply the stated acceptable-with-no-tradeline-overlay treatment.

## Step
If there are 2 or fewer scores, check for either 2 tradelines & 24 month history or 3 tradelines & 12 month history.

## Step
If there is 1 or No Score / Deficient Tradelines, check each of the three printed entries: Max 65% LTV/CLTV; DSCR Ratio ≥ 1.1; 24mos 0x30 housing history.

## Step
Verify that scores & tradelines are reported under the correct ITIN or SSN.

## Step
If FICO is < 620, verify 12 months of reserves.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- Applicants with scores from 3 repositories are treated as acceptable with no tradeline overlay.
- For applicants with 2 or fewer scores, either 2 tradelines & 24 month history or 3 tradelines & 12 month history is met.
- For 1 or No Score / Deficient Tradelines, CLTV is no greater than 65%.
- For 1 or No Score / Deficient Tradelines, DSCR Ratio is ≥ 1.1.
- For 1 or No Score / Deficient Tradelines, 24mos 0x30 housing history is met.
- Scores & tradelines are reported under the correct ITIN or SSN.
- If FICO is < 620, reserves are at least 12 months.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable check holds.
- **Conditional**: A required tradeline, DSCR Ratio, housing-history, or ITIN/SSN report item is not available for review.
- **Fail**: An applicable credit requirement or overlay does not hold.
- **Not Applicable**: the job does not apply to this case

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- If a short sale, deed-in-lieu, or modification applies, its printed seasoning band permits the case: ≥ 24 Mo is No Restrictions; 12-23 Mo has a maximum CLTV of 80% Purchase or 75% Refi R/T, Refi C/O; < 12 Mo has a maximum CLTV of 75% Purchase or 70% Refi R/T, Refi C/O.

values.skill: Apply each stated minimum DSCR, reserve, and property restriction when its listed situation applies.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Apply each stated minimum DSCR, reserve, and property restriction when its listed situation applies. - Base Version

## Purpose

Check the ratio-dependent minimums and restrictions collected in the program provisions.

## Step
Determine which stated situations apply: LTV above 80.00%; loan amount over $2,000,000; 1 or no score / deficient tradelines; rural / unique property; non-warrantable condo or condotel / PUDtel; first-time homebuyer; vacant property refinance purpose; property listed for sale within six months; or mixed use, adult care or assisted living.

## Step
For each applicable situation, compare DSCR with the stated minimum.

## Step
For LTV above 80.00%, also check the stated 6 months PITIA reserves and property-type limitation: SFR, Warrantable Condos outside of Florida, Townhome, PUD.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- If LTV is above 80.00%, DSCR is at least 1.20.
- If LTV is above 80.00%, reserves are 6 months PITIA.
- If LTV is above 80.00%, the property is limited to SFR, Warrantable Condos outside of Florida, Townhome, PUD.
- If the loan amount is over $2,000,000, DSCR is at least 1.0.
- If there is 1 or no score / deficient tradelines, DSCR is at least 1.1.
- If the property is rural / unique, DSCR is at least 1.00.
- If the property is a non-warrantable condo; condotel / PUDtel, DSCR is at least 1.0.
- If the borrower is a first-time homebuyer, DSCR is at least 1.150.
- If the property is vacant and the transaction is a rate & term refinance, DSCR is at least 1.000 (“OR Maximum 40.0% DTI”).
- If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, DSCR is at least 1.15.
- If the property was listed for sale within six months, DSCR is at least 1.0 (“or (b) 43% maximum DTI”).
- If the property is mixed use, adult care or assisted living, DSCR is at least 1.2.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable step is met and every applicable check holds.
- **Conditional**: The applicable requirements are met, subject to conditions that must be cleared.
- **Fail**: A required step is not met or an applicable check does not hold.
- **Not Applicable**: None of the listed situations applies.

# Apply the stated DSCR formula without substituting other rent or payment measures. - Base Version

## Purpose

Calculate the DSCR for a file where a ratio is calculated.

## Step
Identify annual in-place rent and market rent.

## Step
Use the lesser of those rent amounts as the numerator.

## Step
Determine the denominator from annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees; include subordinate financing if applicable.

## Step
Use the first payment due under the terms of the Note, then calculate the ratio.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The numerator is the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent.
- The denominator includes annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees, plus subordinate financing if applicable.
- The calculation uses the first payment due under the terms of the Note.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable step is met and every check holds.
- **Conditional**: The calculation is otherwise met, subject to conditions that must be cleared.
- **Fail**: A required step is not met or a check does not hold.
- **Not Applicable**: The file does not require a calculated DSCR.

# Check the due diligence timing and the persons and entities whose backgrounds Acra reviews under §6.3. - Base Version

## Purpose

values.skill: Verify the required entity documents, their contents, and applicable conditional documentation under §6.2.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify the required entity documents, their contents, and applicable conditional documentation under §6.2. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the entity borrower has provided the entity documentation required without exception and whether applicable conditional documents or additional information are required.

## Step
Confirm that the complete, legible Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments are provided.

## Step
For LLCs and Partnerships, confirm the complete Operating Agreement with all referenced exhibits and all amendments is provided; for corporations, confirm the complete Bylaws with all referenced exhibits and all amendments are provided.

## Step
Confirm the Operating Agreement or Bylaws states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers.

## Step
If the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict, determine whether additional information is required.

## Step
Confirm documentation evidencing all ownership interests is provided in the form specified for the entity type.

## Step
For S or C Corporations, confirm the applicable shareholder / stockholder certificates or stock ledger and any required Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate are provided and account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation.

## Step
For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, confirm the specified K-1 statements and CPA or Tax Preparer letter are provided.

## Step
Confirm names on the entity documents match the identification, or, if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation addresses the discrepancy.

## Step
Confirm a Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document is valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

## Step
If the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located, confirm a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted is provided.

## Step
Confirm the entity's IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter is provided; if an EIN exception is requested, confirm it is submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

## Step
Confirm a Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest authorizes the transaction with Acra Lending and identifies who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity.

## Step
Confirm a Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution is not used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee.

## Step
If a principal uses an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee, confirm a Power of Attorney is utilized by the principal to designate that attorney in fact.

## Step
Do not accept borrower letters stating required documents are not required, available, or excused from providing them; note that Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- A complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto is provided.
- The applicable Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, is complete with all referenced exhibits, legible, and includes all amendments.
- The Operating Agreement or Bylaws states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers.
- Any additional information required because the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict is provided.
- All documentation evidencing ownership interests is provided.
- For LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement identifies, or attaches as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement are provided.
- For S or C Corporations, shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger is provided.
- For S or C Corporations, the certificate or ledger accounts for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation.
- If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is provided.
- For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest is provided.
- For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest is provided, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.
- Names on the entity documents match the identification, or a letter of explanation addresses any failure to match exactly.
- A Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document is valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.
- If the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located, a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted is provided.
- The entity's IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter is provided, or an EIN exception request is submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.
- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest authorizes the transaction with Acra Lending.
- The Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution identifies who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity.
- The Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution is not used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee.
- If a principal uses an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee, a Power of Attorney is utilized by the principal to designate the attorney in fact.
- Borrower letters stating that required documents are not required, available, or excused from providing them are not accepted.

## Outcomes

## Purpose

Determine whether an entity borrower, its ownership structure, and its guarantors meet the entity eligibility and guarantee requirements.

## Step
Confirm the transaction is a business purpose transaction for investment properties exclusively.

## Step
Confirm the collateral title is held directly by individual person(s) or by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion.

## Step
Confirm the entity is US formed and based and is not a foreign owned entity.

## Step
Confirm the entity or guarantor type is allowed and is not a prohibited type.

For an entity borrower, confirm it is a single purpose entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties and that it is engaged in owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.

## Step
Confirm the entity borrower is not a series limited liability company.

## Step
Confirm every entity that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and be on title as a direct owner is a borrowing entity.

## Step
Confirm any business entity nesting is limited to one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary owned by individual(s), with no multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera.

## Step
Confirm all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7).

## Step
If there are multiple guarantors, confirm all recourse is joint and several.

## Step
Confirm changes to the operating agreement or bylaws intended to change ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors are not considered; changes within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process will not be recognized by Acra Lending.

## Step
Confirm at least one guarantor has prior homeownership experience.

## Step
Confirm at least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan attests on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, note that the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation.

- The transaction is a business purpose transaction for investment properties exclusively.
- Title to the collateral is held either directly by individual person(s) or by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion.
- The entity is US formed and based and is not a foreign owned entity.
- The entity or guarantor type is among Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp), single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC) excluding series LLC, Limited Liability Partnership (LLP), Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP), General Partnership (GP), Limited Partnership (LP), or Sole Proprietorship, and is not a Cooperative, Irrevocable Trust, Land Trust, IRA, Non-Profit, or Joint Venture.

- The entity borrower is engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.
- The entity borrower is not a series limited liability company.
- Every entity that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and be on title as a direct owner is a borrowing entity.
- Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn is owned by individual(s), with no multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera.
- All individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7).
- All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors.
- Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors are not considered.
- Changes to ownership percentages within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process are not recognized by Acra Lending.
- At least one guarantor has prior homeownership experience.
- At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan attests on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer.

## Purpose

Determine whether title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust meets each stated requirement.

## Step

## Step
Confirm the Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

Confirm the Trust is established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly, and becomes effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

If the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same, confirm written exception by Acra Senior Management is obtained.

Confirm the Trust contains each required provision concerning the Trustee's power, beneficiary consent, lender rights, and title.

Note that Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust or a Certification of Trust states the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust specifies that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage.
- The Trust specifies that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights.
- The Trust specifies that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

# Identify each stated reserve trigger and verify its printed reserve requirement without supplying unstated bases or cumulative rules. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the reserve requirements stated for applicable loan, borrower, and property circumstances are met.

## Step
Determine whether LTV is > 80.00%; if so, verify 6 months PITIA reserves.

## Step
Determine whether FICO is < 620; if so, apply the stated 12 Months reserve requirement without assuming a payment basis not stated in the source.

## Step
For a first-time homebuyer, verify Minimum six months reserves (“Requires 6mos Reserves”).

## Step
For a vacant property, determine whether the transaction is a rate & term refinance or cash-out refinance and apply the corresponding stated minimum six months reserves or 6 months reserves.

## Step
If the property was listed for sale within six months, verify Twenty-four (24) months of reserves; cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide.

## Step
For forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, where the subject is tenant-occupied and the prior two months' rent were not timely received, verify 12 months of the subject's payment in reserve; this may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand.

## Step
If rent loss insurance is required but cannot be obtained, verify Two (2) months reserves for every one (1) month of coverage not provided.

## Step
Do not infer a base reserve requirement, a payment basis where only “months” is stated, permitted sources, whether overlapping triggers are cumulative, or whether reserves substituted for rent loss insurance are additional; Acra confirmation is requested in Q-07.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- If LTV is > 80.00%, 6 months PITIA reserves are held.
- If FICO is < 620, the stated 12 Months reserve requirement is met; its payment basis is not specified in the source.
- A first-time homebuyer has Minimum six months reserves (“Requires 6mos Reserves”).
- For a vacant property — rate & term refinance, Minimum six months reserves are held.
- For a vacant property — cash-out refinance, 6 months reserves are held.
- If the property was listed for sale within six months, Twenty-four (24) months of reserves are held, with cash-in-hand considered only if otherwise consistent with the Guide.
- If forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, tenant-occupied subject, and no timely receipt of the prior two months' rent all apply, 12 months of the subject's payment are held in reserve; the reserve may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand.
- If rent loss insurance is required but cannot be obtained, Two (2) months reserves are held for every one (1) month of coverage not provided.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable step is met and every check holds.
- **Conditional**: A requirement remains subject to conditions that must be cleared.

## Purpose

## Step

If loan_amount is greater than $2,000,000, verify that DSCR is 1.0 or greater.

## Step

If delayed financing applies, apply the stated $1.5MM cap.

## Step
For Cash-Out, where LTV is greater than 65%, apply footnote 1: maximum cash-in-hand is $1,000,000 for loans ≥ $1,500,000 and $500,000 for loans < $1,500,000.

## Step
Note footnote 2 as printed: “When LTV ≤ 65%, unlimited cash-in-hand allowed”. The source requests Acra confirmation on whether footnote 2 applies to every tier or only the tier bearing its marker, and why the footnotes use LTV while the matrix is labelled CLTV.

- If loan_amount is less than $200,000 and loan_purpose is Rate & Term or Cash-Out, cltv_pct is no more than 75%.

- If the loan is interest-only, loan_amount is no more than $3,000,000.
- If the loan is interest-only, fico is at least 640.
- If delayed financing applies, loan_amount is no more than $1.5MM.
- If the loan is Cash-Out and LTV is greater than 65%, cash-in-hand is no more than the applicable footnote 1 cap.
- The applicable treatment of footnote 2 and the LTV-versus-CLTV footnotes is confirmed where needed.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable condition is met and every applicable check holds.
- **Conditional**: Applicable conditions that can be evaluated are met, subject to required data or Acra confirmations that must be cleared.
- **Fail**: An applicable step is not met or an applicable check does not hold.

For a minimum whose interaction with a state restriction needs confirmation, request Acra confirmation as indicated by Q-24.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The case is a vacant-property rate & term refinance.
- The case is a vacant-property cash-out refinance.
- The property is listed for sale.
- If the case is a vacant-property rate & term refinance, the selected term is at least two years where allowable.
- If the case is a vacant-property cash-out refinance, the selected term is at least three years where allowable.
- If the property is listed for sale and is not located in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties, the selected term is at least three years.
- Any applicable state-restriction interaction with a minimum term has the Acra confirmation requested by Q-24.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable minimum term is met and any applicable state-restriction interaction has the confirmation requested by Q-24.
- **Conditional**: An applicable term, “where allowable” determination, state exception, or state-interaction confirmation remains unresolved.
- **Fail**: An applicable minimum term is not met.
- **Not Applicable**: None of the specified transaction types applies.

values.skill: Compare the selected prepayment penalty term and structure with the structures printed in STD-11.1.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Compare the selected prepayment penalty term and structure with the structures printed in STD-11.1. - Base Version

## Step

Verify that it matches one of the options printed for that term in STD-11.1, including “No Prepay” as a listed structure.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The selected prepayment penalty term and structure match an option printed for that term in STD-11.1.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The selected term and structure match an option printed for that term in STD-11.1.
- **Conditional**: The selected term or structure is not available to review.
- **Fail**: The selected term and structure do not match an option printed for that term in STD-11.1.
